title: Waylight documentation
summary: Waylight is a self-hosted start page for one person and, if you like, the people they share a home with. You arrange widgets on tabs: the weather, your calendar and to-dos next to the state of your home server, its containers and its …

title: What Waylight is and is not
summary: This page is for deciding whether Waylight is worth installing. It describes the ideas behind the project, what you need to run it and where it falls short today.

title: Absences
summary: With a licence key that includes absences (licence keys), everyone on the instance can see who is away: on holiday, sick, working remotely or away for another reason. This needs a server built with the ee features.

title: Accessibility
summary: Waylight aims for WCAG 2.2 level AA (#113). Everything can be used with a keyboard and a screen reader.

title: Accounts, guests and kiosk displays
summary: Waylight has one owner, who can change everything. The owner can let other people and devices look at selected tabs: guests sign in with their own password, kiosk displays with a secret link. Neither can change anything. This page covers …

title: Adding a module
summary: A module is a feature with its own backend rings, frontend feature folder, settings, documentation and tests. This page is the reference for what a module consists of. If you would rather learn by building one, follow the developer guide, …

title: Admin policies
summary: With a licence key that includes policies (licence keys), admins set rules that hold for every account. This needs a server built with the ee features.

title: Announcements
summary: With a licence key that includes announcements (licence keys), admins post short notices for everyone on the instance, such as "The office is closed on Friday". This needs a server built with the ee features.

title: API tokens
summary: Personal API tokens let scripts and automations use the Waylight API without a browser session: iOS Shortcuts, Home Assistant, cron jobs.

title: Appearance
summary: Settings → Appearance controls how the dashboard looks and which language it speaks. Settings are stored on the server, so every browser you sign in with looks the same.

title: Phones, offline use and the browser extension
summary: Waylight is a web page, but it can behave like an app: installed on your phone's home screen, readable without a connection and opened on every new browser tab. This page explains what each of these needs.

title: Architecture
summary: Waylight is a single Go binary that serves a JSON API and an embedded Svelte single-page application. Both halves follow Clean Architecture (see ADR 0001).

title: Audit log
summary: With a licence key that includes audit-log (licence keys), Waylight records who changed shared data and settings, when, and which object. It never records the content: the log says that a service was changed, not what it is called now.

title: Backups and restore
summary: Everything Waylight knows lives in one SQLite database. This page explains what is backed up automatically, how to keep a copy away from the server and how to restore it. The examples use Docker Compose; the Raspberry Pi and native install …

title: Branding
summary: With a licence key that includes branding (licence keys), admins give the instance their organisation's name, logos, favicon and colours. This needs a server built with the ee features.

title: How Waylight compares
summary: Last reviewed: 2026-11-14 for Waylight, 2026-11-11 for the others (Homarr v2.12.0, Homepage v2.8.0, Glance v0.8.8, Dashy 4.9.0). Reviewed with every minor release of Waylight — corrections are very welcome as an issue or pull request.

title: Settings as a YAML file
summary: Waylight can write its settings into one readable file, waylight.yaml, and read them back. Keep that file in Git, review changes before you apply them, or set up a second instance the same way as the first. This page explains what the file …

title: Configuration reference
summary: Waylight reads its configuration from environment variables when it starts. Everything that only you as the signed-in owner should decide, such as service tiles, calendars or notification channels, lives in the web interface instead. …

title: Connected accounts
summary: With a licence key that includes connected-accounts (licence keys), each member can connect their own account at Microsoft 365, Confluence (Atlassian Cloud), Notion or Slack. The team integrations, such as wiki and chat search, then act on …

title: Tabs and widgets
summary: Everything you see in Waylight is a widget on a tab. This page explains how to arrange them, how the phone layout works and how to make a tab open by itself. For a guided first run, see first steps.

title: Licence keys
summary: The features in ee/ (team tabs, single sign-on with groups, branding and the others listed in ADR 0020) work only with a licence key. Everything else in Waylight needs no key. This page explains how a key is checked and how to enter one.

title: Prometheus metrics
summary: Waylight can expose its measurements at GET /metrics in the Prometheus text format, so an existing Prometheus/Grafana setup can scrape them. The endpoint is off by default.

title: JSON widget

title: arr (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr)
summary: What it does: Sonarr, Radarr and Prowlarr in one widget (several instances): upcoming episodes and movies for two weeks, download queue with progress and stuck downloads, health warnings and the number of missing items.

title: Birthdays

title: Family board
summary: What it does: Short notes for everyone in the household, which can be pinned and can expire on a chosen day.

title: Calendar
summary: What it does: Shows your appointments as an agenda, a month or a split view with event details, and lets you add events from the widget. Events come from CalDAV calendars (Nextcloud, Radicale, Baïkal, Fastmail, …), read-only ICS …

title: Chores
summary: What it does: Recurring household tasks with the people who take turns, a done button and a compact view that says how many tasks are due today.

title: Contracts
summary: What it does: Household contracts with their cost and cancellation deadline, and a reminder through your notification channels before each deadline.

title: Device (display mode)
summary: What it does: On the Raspberry Pi appliance image (ADR 0015), you choose whether the Pi is only a server or also shows the dashboard full-screen on a connected display: HDMI or the official touch display (#140). Docker and plain .deb …

title: Warranty and documents
summary: What it does: Keeps receipts and warranty papers with the product, shows how long each warranty runs, and stores the photo or PDF on your Waylight server.

title: Drop zone
summary: What it does: Share text, links and small files between your devices (#101). Paste or drop something on one device and pick it up on another. Items are listed newest first with copy and download buttons and expire automatically after 1 …

title: Electricity prices

title: Fuel prices
summary: What it does: Fuel prices in Germany from Tankerkönig (MTS-K data, CC BY 4.0): the cheapest open stations around a place for E5, E10 or Diesel, or your favourite stations.

title: Game deals
summary: What it does: Discounts on your public Steam wishlist (price, discount, end date, minimum discount) and the current free games of the Epic Games Store.

title: Gift ideas
summary: What it does: Private gift ideas per person, grouped by person and sorted by the next birthday when the birthdays module is on.

title: Grafana
summary: What it does: panels and alerts of your Grafana on the dashboard. The Grafana panel widget shows one panel as an image, rendered by Grafana; the Grafana alerts widget lists the firing and pending alerts of Grafana Alerting. Waylight talks …

title: Habits
summary: What it does: Habit tracker widget: daily habits or chosen weekdays, one tap to check off today (or yesterday), current and best streak, and an optional 4-week heatmap. Days off do not break a streak.

title: Holidays
summary: What it does: The next public holidays of a German state, with weekday and a countdown, and optionally the school holidays (#55). The state is chosen per widget (default: Lower Saxony); current holidays are highlighted.

title: Immich
summary: What it does: Immich photo library on the dashboard: number of photos and videos, storage, and today's "on this day" memories. Thumbnails are proxied by Waylight, so the API key never reaches the browser.

title: Integrations
summary: What it does: an admin saves the address and the credential of a service once, as a named connection such as "Home" or "Office", and widgets of that service choose it. A service can have several connections, for example two Proxmox …

title: Mail
summary: What it does: Shows how many unread messages are waiting and lists the newest ones (sender, subject, time) of one or more IMAP inboxes. A click opens your webmail (#283).

title: Markets
summary: What it does: A small watchlist: currencies, shares, indices and crypto with the latest value, the change against the previous close and a 30-day sparkline (#284).

title: Meal plan
summary: What it does: A week of dishes for the household, each with an optional meal, a recipe link and ingredients that go onto the shopping list with one click.

title: Media server (Jellyfin, Plex)
summary: What it does: Jellyfin or Plex: what is playing right now (user, device, progress) and recently added movies, episodes and albums with posters. Posters are proxied by Waylight, so the token stays on the server.

title: Meter readings
summary: What it does: Keeps the readings of your electricity, gas, water and heat meters and shows how much you used per month and per year.

title: Phone list
summary: What it does: a searchable directory of the people in your organisation or household, with name, role, team, phone number and e-mail address. Numbers and addresses are links, so a click calls or writes.

title: Photo frame
summary: What it does: Shows your own pictures one after another, like a digital photo frame. The pictures are uploaded to Waylight itself, so no photo server is needed (#286). If you run Immich, the Immich widget shows pictures from there instead.

title: Places
summary: What it does: you enter a place once, by address search or with your browser's location, and choose it in every widget that needs a location.

title: Read later
summary: What it does: A read-later list (#99). Save a web page and Waylight stores a cleaned reader copy (article text, headings, lists, quotes, code, tables, links and the article's images). The copy stays readable when the page changes or …

title: Releases
summary: What it does: New albums, singles and EPs of the artists you follow, from MusicBrainz, with cover art from the Cover Art Archive.

title: Shopping list
summary: What it does: a shopping list on the start page. Keep the list on Waylight and share it with the people you shop for, or connect a CalDAV task list that everyone already uses in their task app.

title: Space
summary: What it does: The next rocket launches (rocket, mission, local time, status) from Launch Library 2 and NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day with title and explanation (#64).

title: Sports
summary: What it does: Follows a football team: its last result, the next fixture and its place in the table. Without a team the widget shows the top of the league table (#285).

title: Study progress
summary: What it does: A manually maintained list of your study modules with ECTS, semester, status (open, in progress, passed) and grade (#57). The widget shows the passed credits as a progress bar against the credits of the whole degree, the …

title: AI summaries (Ollama)
summary: What it does: Summarises notes and feed articles in 3–5 bullet points with a local Ollama (#75). Nothing leaves your home network.

title: Native install (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS)
summary: Waylight is a single static binary, so it does not need Docker. Every release attaches .deb packages for amd64 and arm64 that install it as a hardened systemd service. This is also what the Raspberry Pi image is built from (ADR 0015).

title: Notifications and job monitoring
summary: Waylight can tell you when something needs attention: a service goes offline, a disk fills up, a certificate is about to expire, a backup did not run. This page explains how to set up the channels, how to keep alerts quiet when they should …

title: Outbound requests
summary: Waylight sends no telemetry and contacts no server of its own. It only talks to services you set up or switch on. This page lists every outside connection, when it happens and how often, so you can check the claim and plan your firewall.

title: Parcels from shipping e-mails
summary: The parcels widget can find tracking numbers in your shipping e-mails by itself (#166). Waylight reads one folder of your mailbox over IMAP and adds every new parcel it finds.

title: Microsoft Teams
summary: With a licence key that includes chat-apps (licence keys), Waylight works with Microsoft Teams in two ways, both set up by your own admins with your own Microsoft registrations (ADR 0023). This needs a server built with the ee features.

title: Updates and rollback
summary: New releases are listed with their changes on the releases page. Settings → About shows the version you run and, if you turn on the update check, whether a newer one exists. The check asks the GitHub API at most once a day.
